title: Sulfur burps on GLP-1s and what you can try | Nerva
summary: Practical steps for sulfur burps while taking a GLP-1, what to know about Pepto-Bismol and probiotics, and when to get medical help.
body_markdown:
Burping and diarrhea can both occur during GLP-1 treatment. Infections and other digestive problems can also cause the combination, especially if it starts suddenly or someone around you is ill.


The[CDC lists gas and diarrhea among Giardia symptoms](https://www.cdc.gov/giardia/about/) , for example. Recent travel, untreated drinking water, or greasy, foul-smelling stools are details to mention to your clinician. Sulfur burps alone don't diagnose an infection or tell you whether you need testing.


Replace fluid and electrolyte losses from diarrhea.[NIDDK's treatment guidance](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/digestive-diseases/diarrhea/treatment) includes oral rehydration solutions; a pharmacist can help you choose one. Get individual advice about fluids if you have diabetes, kidney disease or a fluid restriction.


[Contact a doctor right away](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/digestive-diseases/diarrhea/symptoms-causes) for diarrhea lasting more than two days, six or more loose stools in a day, or high fever. Seek help sooner for dehydration or severe symptoms.


Our[GLP-1 diarrhea guide](https://www.nervahealth.com/post/glp-1-diarrhea) has more on fluid losses. If your bowel movements have instead become difficult or infrequent, see the[constipation guide](https://www.nervahealth.com/post/glp-1-constipation) .


## How long do sulfur burps last?


Research hasn't given sulfur burps a reliable timeline. General digestive symptoms often occur when treatment starts or the dose increases. Some become less frequent over time, but nausea and diarrhea studies can't tell you when sulfur odor will disappear.


If the burps keep coming back, interfere with meals or wake you at night, arrange a prescriber appointment. Note when they started and whether they followed a prescribed change. Include any vomiting, pain or bowel changes, and say whether you're eating and drinking normally.


Our[guide to GLP-1 side-effect timelines](https://www.nervahealth.com/post/how-long-glp-1-side-effects-last) explains the difference between a brief episode and symptoms that recur over several weeks.


## Where gut-brain support fits


Some frequent belching comes from air moving into and out of the esophagus, called supragastric belching. The[AGA includes brain-gut behavioral therapies](https://gastro.org/clinical-guidance/evaluation-and-management-of-belching-abdominal-bloating-and-distention/) among the options for this diagnosed problem. A clinician can distinguish it from other types of belching.


For ongoing digestive concerns, Nerva offers daily gut-directed hypnotherapy and breathing exercises focused on how you respond to gut sensations. Its trial evidence is in IBS; it hasn't been shown to treat GLP-1 sulfur burps.


Read about[gut-brain approaches](https://www.nervahealth.com/post/glp-1-gut-brain-connection) or[explore Nerva](https://www.nervahealth.com/glp-1) .


> **When to get medical help**
>
>
> **Call 911** for chest pain, trouble breathing, fainting or collapse.
>
>
> **Get medical help right away** for severe or lasting abdominal pain, especially if it spreads to your back; vomiting blood or black or bloody stools; repeated vomiting, inability to keep fluids down or very little urine; a swollen, painful belly with inability to pass stool or gas; or upper-right abdominal pain with fever or yellow skin or eyes.
>
>
> Trouble swallowing needs prompt medical assessment. If you can't swallow at all, go to an emergency department.
>
>
> Sources:[medication warnings](https://www.novo-pi.com/wegovy.pdf) ,[NIDDK](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/digestive-diseases/gastroparesis/symptoms-causes) ,[CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/heart-disease/about/heart-attack.html) and[Mayo Clinic](https://www.mayoclinic.org/symptom-checker/difficulty-swallowing-in-adults-adult/related-factors/itt-20009075) .
